Hi Sarah — appreciate the details. I laid out our typical exception workflow and two pragmatic options we usually recommend for high-volume nightly jobs:

Option A — Reserved Dedicated Window (recommended for strict completion windows)
- Redwood reserves a dedicated GPU pool for your nightly window (e.g., 10pm–4am PT).
- Completion SLA measured from job submission to final ack: 4 hours SLO with a 99% success target per calendar month.
- Fallback policy: if capacity is constrained, we route to a compatible model variant (slower/cheaper) and notify your on-call.
- Compensation: SLA credit schedule (tiered) — we can draft financial language for the contract addendum.

Option B — Best-effort with priority routing
- No dedicated capacity; jobs are prioritized in the shared pool during your window.
- Completion target: best-effort with operational alerts at 95th percentile breach.

Idempotency and retries (applies to both options)
- We require a client-provided batch_id (string) for each submission; Redwood will dedupe based on batch_id for 7 days by default.
- Retry behavior: at-least-once delivery is the baseline. For exactly-once semantics, we recommend using batch-level dedupe + idempotent downstream consumers.
- Retries: exponential backoff with jitter implemented server-side; clients may retry on 5xx with a recommended cap of 5 automatic retries.

Hi team — a few technical notes to make the SLA measurable and implementable:

Measurement window definition
- "Submission time" = timestamp when Redwood's API returns 202 Accepted for the job POST (this includes basic validation).
- "Completion time" = timestamp when last output shard for the job is written to the configured push sink (S3/pubsub) and job status transitions to COMPLETED.

Idempotency and dedupe
- Include a stable batch_id (UUID) and per-record id within the payload. Redwood stores a compact index of recent batch_ids for 7 days; if a duplicate batch_id is seen, the service returns a 200 with a reference to prior job run (no reprocessing).
- For very large runs we also recommend chunking (e.g., 100k record chunks) with chunk_id to allow partial retries and faster recovery.

Retries and failure semantics
- Server-side retries: transient infra errors trigger server retries with backoff (initial 2s, factor 2, jitter, max 5 retries).
- Client retries: clients should retry on 429/503 with an increasing backoff; include Idempotency-Key header to avoid double-processing.
- At-least-once delivery remains the safe default; exactly-once requires client-side dedupe or an idempotent sink.

Operational instrumentation we recommend exposing in the contract:
- Metrics: job_submission_ts, job_first_worker_start_ts, job_last_worker_end_ts, job_completion_ts, records_processed, failed_records, retry_count.
- Alerts: job duration > 3.5 hours (warning), > 4 hours (critical).

Sample SLA clause (draft wording)
"Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that 99% of Customer's designated nightly batch jobs (as identified by batch_id) submitted during the Customer's reserved window will reach COMPLETED status within four (4) hours of submission. Failure to meet the foregoing service level will entitle Customer to service credits as set forth in the SLA addendum."

I'll attach a short runbook (nightly-batch-runbook.md) with recommended operational checks and remediation steps.

- Rishi
Senior Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference
